numberHierarchy.title: Number Hierarchy

hints.build: click a point or a row name, or play to fill the rows from the bottom
hints.disguised: click a number, or play to check them one by one

intro.build: every row holds all the points of the rows below it. From bottom to top the line gets fuller, then $\mathbb{C}$ leaves the line.
intro.disguised: the way a number is written can fool you. Simplify it first, then find the lowest row that holds it.

build.natural: the primes, $1$ and the composites make up $\mathbb{N}$.

about.natural: $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$ is made of the primes $\mathbb{P}=\{2,3,5,7,\dots\}$, the number $1$ and the composites $\mathbb{K}=\{4,6,8,9,\dots\}$.
about.rational: $\mathbb{Q}$ is $\mathbb{Z}$ plus fractions such as $\tfrac12$ and $-\tfrac23$. Every rational number can be written as $\tfrac{m}{n}$ with $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$, $n\neq 0$.
about.real: $\mathbb{R}$ is $\mathbb{Q}$ plus the irrational numbers $\mathbb{I}_r$, such as $\sqrt2$, $e$ and $\pi$. Its line is whole, with no gaps.
about.complex: $\mathbb{C}=\{a+bi\mid a,b\in\mathbb{R},\ i^2=-1\}$. A real number is a complex number with $b=0$, for example $3=3+0i$, so it sits on the line. What gets added: the numbers with $b\neq 0$, off the line.

reasons.one: $1$ is neither prime nor composite, so it has its own part of $\mathbb{N}$.
reasons.two: $2$ is divisible only by $1$ and $2$: a prime.
reasons.three: $3$ is divisible only by $1$ and $3$: a prime.
reasons.zero: $0$ is not a natural number. It first appears in $\mathbb{C}_a$.
reasons.negative: a negative integer, which first appears in $\mathbb{Z}$.
reasons.fraction: a fraction that is not an integer, which first appears in $\mathbb{Q}$.
reasons.sqrtTwo: $\sqrt2$ cannot be written as $\tfrac{m}{n}$: an irrational number. In the $\mathbb{Q}$ row its place is still a gap.
reasons.pi: $\pi=3.14159\dots$ has decimals that never stop and never repeat: an irrational number. In the $\mathbb{Q}$ row its place is still a gap.
reasons.imaginaryUnit: $i=0+1i$, so $a=0$ and $b=1$. Since $b\neq 0$, the point leaves the real line, $1$ unit up.
reasons.onePlusTwoI: $a=1$ and $b=2$: $1$ unit right, $2$ units up. Since $b\neq 0$, it is not a real number.
reasons.sixThirds: looks like a fraction, but $6\div 3=2$: a prime.
reasons.sqrtNine: has a root sign, but $3\times 3=9$, so $\sqrt9=3$: a prime.
reasons.minusEightQuarters: $-8\div 4=-2$: a negative integer, not a fraction.
reasons.iSquared: has an $i$, but $i^2=-1$ by definition: a negative integer.
reasons.threeQuarters: a terminating decimal: $0.75=\tfrac{75}{100}=\tfrac34$, so it is rational.
reasons.repeating: a repeating decimal is rational too: let $x=0.333\dots$, then $10x-x=3$, so $x=\tfrac13$.
reasons.sqrtEight: $\sqrt8=2\sqrt2$, and $\sqrt2$ is irrational, so $\sqrt8$ is irrational too.
reasons.sqrtMinusFour: no real number squares to $-4$. $\sqrt{-4}=2i$, because $(2i)^2=4i^2=-4$.

note.notBelow: but ${{value}}\notin {{set}}$, so it is not in any lower row.

numberHierarchy.membershipFootnote: read each column: once a number is $\in$ a set, it stays $\in$ further down.

complexNumbers.title: Complex Numbers

plot.intro: a complex number $z = a + bi$ is drawn as the point $(a, b)$: the real part $a$ on the horizontal axis $\mathrm{Re}(z)$, the imaginary part $b$ on the vertical axis $\mathrm{Im}(z)$.
plot.summary: every $z = a + bi$ has exactly one point $(a, b)$ in the plane, and every point has exactly one $z$.
plot.hint: click a point, or play to draw them one by one.
captions: $z_1 = 1 + 2i$: 1 to the right along $\mathrm{Re}(z)$, then 2 up. The point is $(1, 2)$.
$z_2 = -2 + i$: 2 to the left, then 1 up. The point is $(-2, 1)$.
$z_3 = -1 - 2i$: 1 to the left, then 2 down. The point is $(-1, -2)$.
$z_4 = 2 - i$: 2 to the right, then 1 down. The point is $(2, -1)$.

add.intro: real adds to real, imaginary to imaginary. In the plane: start at $z_1$, then walk as far as $z_2$.
add.summary: $z_1 + z_2 = 3 - i$. Adding means joining: the walk of $z_2$ (2 right, 3 down) is attached to the end of $z_1$.
add.hint: click a point, or play to add part by part.
captions: real part: $1 + 2 = 3$. From $z_1$ move 2 to the right.
imaginary part: $2 + (-3) = -1$. Move 3 down.

subtract.intro: real minus real, imaginary minus imaginary. In the plane: start at $z_1$, then walk as far as $z_2$ in the opposite direction.
subtract.summary: $z_1 - z_2 = -1 + 5i$. Subtracting $z_2$ is walking as far as $z_2$ the other way: 2 left, 3 up.
subtract.hint: click a point, or play to subtract part by part.
captions: real part: $1 - 2 = -1$. From $z_1$ move 2 to the left.
imaginary part: $2 - (-3) = 5$. Move 3 up.

multiply.intro: every term times every term, like $(a + b)(c + d)$. The difference: $i \cdot i = i^2 = -1$, so imaginary times imaginary moves to the real part.
multiply.summary: $z_1 \cdot z_2 = 8 + i$. The term $2i \cdot (-3i)$ looks imaginary, but $i^2 = -1$ makes it real: 6 to the right, not up.
multiply.hint: click a point, or play to fill the boxes one by one.
captions: $1 \cdot 2 = 2$, real. From 0 move 2 to the right.
$1 \cdot (-3i) = -3i$, imaginary. Move 3 down, right onto $z_2$, because $1 \cdot z_2 = z_2$.
$2i \cdot 2 = 4i$, imaginary. Move 4 up.
$2i \cdot (-3i) = -6i^2 = 6$, because $i^2 = -1$. So it is real: move 6 to the right.
real $2 + 6 = 8$, imaginary $-3i + 4i = i$. So $z_1 \cdot z_2 = 8 + i$.

divide.intro: multiply the top and the bottom by the conjugate of the bottom, $\bar{z}_2$. The bottom becomes a real number, then each part is simply divided.
divide.hint: click a point, or play to divide step by step.
captions: conjugate of the bottom: $\bar{z}_2 = 2 + 3i$, the mirror of $z_2$ in the $\mathrm{Re}(z)$ axis.
bottom: $(2 - 3i)(2 + 3i) = 4 + 9 = 13$. The imaginary part cancels, so it is real.
divide by 13: $\tfrac{z_1}{z_2} = -\tfrac{4}{13} + \tfrac{7}{13}i$. Same direction as $-4 + 7i$, 13 times closer to 0.

conjugate.intro: the conjugate of $z = a + bi$ is $\bar{z} = a - bi$: the imaginary part changes sign. In the plane: a mirror in the $\mathrm{Re}(z)$ axis.
conjugate.summary: conjugate = mirror in the $\mathrm{Re}(z)$ axis. That is why $\overline{z_1 - z_2} = \bar{z}_1 - \bar{z}_2$: both are the point $(-1, -5)$.
conjugate.hint: click a point, or play to mirror them one by one.
captions: $\bar{z}_1 = 1 - 2i$: the mirror of $z_1$ in the $\mathrm{Re}(z)$ axis.
$\bar{z}_2 = 2 + 3i$: the mirror of $z_2$.
$z_1 - z_2 = -1 + 5i$, as on the $z_1 - z_2$ tab.
the mirror of $z_1 - z_2$ lands on the same point: $\overline{z_1 - z_2} = \bar{z}_1 - \bar{z}_2$.

extras.conjugateOfZ2: the mirror of $z_2$ in the $\mathrm{Re}(z)$ axis.
extras.numerator: this is the top, not yet divided by 13.
extras.quotient: it lies on the line from 0 to $-4 + 7i$, 13 times closer to 0.

complexNumbers.twoFormsFootnote: so $(1, 2)$ and $1 + 2i$ are the same number.
complexNumbers.whyIText: $x^2 + 1 = 0$ means $x^2 = -1$. The square of a real number is never negative, so $\mathbb{R}$ has no answer. With $i^2 = -1$, the answers are $x = i$ and $x = -i$.

productTags.footnote: rows from $z_1 = 1 + 2i$, columns from $z_2 = 2 - 3i$. Shaded boxes = real part.
